singles.content: The studio was registered on 14 March 2021 as a private limited company, with the lead as sole director.
Priya works Monday to Thursday, so nothing that needs her lands on a Friday. That has been the arrangement since she joined in April 2025.
My nephew's birthday is 9 December.
Since the 2025 audit, every client contract includes the data-processing annex, signed before work starts.
No client calls on Fridays this July; push requests to Thursday or the following Monday.
Blood type is A negative.
Keep three months of expenses in the savings account and never dip into it for travel.
Submit the talk proposal for the November frontend conference by 15 September; Tomas reviews the abstract first.
Invoices are numbered INV-YYYY-NNNN, and the counter restarts every January; credit notes use CN-YYYY-NNNN.
Raise the partner API rate limit to 600 requests per minute for the bakery client's import weekend, 27 to 28 September, then set it back to the standard plan limit on Monday morning.
The October newsletter should be short and upbeat, with the autumn plan in three lines.
Collect waitlist sign-ups with the landing-page form and export them every Monday to the newsletter tool.
Ran the autumn 10k in 49:05 in heavy rain.
The car insurance renews on 1 June and costs about 540 euros a year, with a 300-euro excess and breakdown cover included.
Wren works in two-week sprints that start on a Monday, with planning that morning and the review on the second Friday.
Internal alpha builds of wren crash in about 1.8% of sessions, mostly on Android 11 phones.
API error messages are plain sentences with a stable machine-readable code; never put stack traces in responses.
The studio closes from 22 December 2025 to 2 January 2026. Support gets an auto-reply for that window, and Lena checks the inbox once, on 29 December.
Keep this December's gift budget to 300 euros in total, and buy the nephew's present before the 5th.
Nothing merges to main without one review, including the lead's own changes. Reviews happen within a working day, and the author merges once the review is in.
Sell the car before the residents' parking permit renews in June, and put the money toward the kitchen.
The site's hosting runs on a 60-day free trial that ends on 7 February.
Nephew's eighth birthday: gave him the bike lights; party at my sister's.
Long runs on Sunday mornings at an easy pace, with the club when possible.
Hold all paid acquisition until launch day. Growth comes from the waitlist and the two newsletter swaps already agreed with other small app makers.
Blog posts are published under CC BY 4.0 and code snippets under the MIT licence.

Follow the 16-week plan for the April half marathon: four runs a week, intervals on Tuesdays, tempo on Thursdays, and a long run on Sundays building to 19 km. Rest days are Monday and Friday, and the week after any cold is run at easy pace only.
The studio's liability insurance covers up to 2 million euros per claim and renews each March.
In the week before the April half marathon, keep dinners plain: pasta or rice, no new foods, no alcohol.
No internal meetings before 10:00 on Mondays; that time is for planning the week and clearing the support queue.
The studio's domains renew every January, and the registrar emails a reminder in early December.

Run the junior developer hiring round in February: interviews on Tuesdays and Wednesdays, two rounds, and a take-home task capped at three hours. Priya writes the task, Tomas joins the second round, and every candidate hears back within five working days.
Physio is at the clinic on Elm Road, Mondays at 08:15, through the end of March.
Five candidates are booked for first interviews between 3 and 12 February.
Do the Spanish course homework on Wednesday evenings, the night before class.
Wren collects no third-party analytics; product metrics come from heron's own event table.
Window seat on trains, aisle seat on flights.
Wren's bundle identifier is studio.wren.app on both app stores, and the signing keys are in the studio's password manager.
January review: ran 142 km, read two books, groceries 40 euros over budget.
The flat lease renews automatically each 1 September unless either side gives three months' notice.
For the February junior interviews, keep the panel to two people so candidates don't face a crowd.
The larkspur contract was signed on 3 February 2026 and runs 18 months, to 2 August 2027.
Larkspur is billed monthly in arrears at the agreed day rate for the full 18-month contract, starting with February 2026.
Dental check-up: no issues; next visit booked for August.
During discovery, interview the dispatch team and at least two captains before any dashboard design work starts.
Keep heron as one service with one database until it needs more than two instances at peak.
Visitors can park in the Harbour Street courtyard if Lena registers their number plate the day before.
During discovery, the ferry client's point of contact is the dispatch lead; the operations director joins only the final readout.
Book the kitchen fitters for the first two weeks of May and stay at my sister's while the water is off.

For the six-week discovery phase starting 16 February, write interview notes as one page per person, with quotes in italics and open questions at the bottom. Share each page with the dispatch lead within a day so corrections come in while the conversation is fresh.
In the Thursday Spanish class, sit with the conversation group rather than at the grammar table.
Hold the Postgres major upgrade until the March release has been out for a week without incidents.
The spring Spanish course meets on Thursdays from 18:30 to 20:00 at the adult education centre, with the last class on 18 June.
The studio newsletter goes out on the first Tuesday of each month, written by the lead and checked by Tomas the Friday before.
Monthly finance check: hardware spend above budget after the two laptops; everything else on plan, and the tax reserve topped up to the quarter's estimate.
While the knee is in physio through March, the Wednesday run becomes a 40-minute swim.
In larkspur documents, call the users dispatchers and crew, never operators, which is the client's word for the company itself.
The Harbour Street meeting room seats eight and has a wall screen with an HDMI cable only.
Next Tuesday's steering-group demo runs from the staging build, not a laptop copy, so the dispatch lead can click through it afterwards.
For the April workshop with the dispatch team, print the agenda on A3 and skip slides entirely.
Beta testers get a new build through the invite link every Thursday afternoon, with a three-line changelog posted in the beta chat.
Retro: agreed to move the daily standup to 09:30 so Priya can do the school run first.
All larkspur data stays in the client's own cloud account. The studio gets read access to the reporting schema only, through named accounts, and nothing is copied to studio laptops or studio storage.
Book physio sessions in the early morning slots until the knee rehab finishes at the end of March.
Nine people from the ferry client confirmed for the 9 April workshop, including two captains and the timetable planner.
Book the Harbour Street meeting room through the landlord's sheet. Client workshops take priority over internal meetings, and bookings over two hours need a note.
Heron outage: 11 minutes of failed logins from a locked sessions table; the migration was rolled back.
The ferry client's booking data arrives as a nightly CSV export at 02:00 local time, dropped into the shared bucket with the previous day's date in the file name.
Outage notes: the migration took a lock on sessions; next time, run long migrations off-peak with a lock timeout.
After the March outage, every schema migration ships with a tested rollback script, and the deploy checklist links to it.
The 9 April workshop is in the ferry terminal's upstairs room. Bring the projector adapter and print name cards.
The 19 March outage came from a migration that locked the sessions table for 11 minutes.
Heron's production database runs in the eu-north region, on the provider's two-node high-availability plan.

The database upgrade window is Saturday 11 April, 22:00 to 02:00 UTC, and the API shows a maintenance banner during it. Writes are refused for the whole window, reads stay up from the replica, and the status page carries the same times.
Week 14 digest: outage follow-ups closed, the redesign is at the mockup stage, and the accountant has the Q1 figures.
No new blog posts from 6 to 24 April while the site redesign is built.
Race numbers for the half marathon are collected at the sports hall on the Friday before, 17:00 to 20:00.
For the 11 to 12 April database upgrade weekend, reach me by phone, not chat.

Workshop with nine dispatch staff: mapped the morning delay process and agreed three dashboard views. The captains asked for the delay reasons to use their own codes, not the booking system's, and for the views to work on the bridge tablets.
Debrief from the 9 April workshop: dispatch wants delays by route first and by vessel second.
For the April redesign, review page mockups in the Tuesday design slot, not in chat threads.
Use the March design for the launch screenshots; Tomas exports them at the three required sizes by 20 May.
Kestrel's three test accounts share the studio's QA mailbox.
Steering meeting: the client approved the dashboard scope and confirmed the budget for the pipeline phase.
Wren has 1,140 beta testers; about 60% open the app at least once a week.
The kitchen fitters arrive on 4 May and need the water shut off from 08:00.
Ran the spring half marathon in 1:52:40, five minutes faster than last year.
Race notes: started too fast, slowed at km 15; gels at km 7 and 14 worked.
The redesigned site is previewed on the sorrel staging domain behind basic auth until go-live on 24 April.
Kestrel syncs saved highlights every 15 minutes while the browser is open, plus on demand from the toolbar button.
Store every timestamp in UTC and convert only at the edge, in the user's locale.
Kestrel's toolbar icon stays monochrome so it sits quietly next to other extensions.
Status updates go in the weekly written update, not in meetings. Each person writes three lines on Friday: done, next, and anything blocking.
Go-live notes: redirects checked, two broken image links fixed, sitemap resubmitted.
The site uses a cookie-free, self-hosted analytics script, so it needs no cookie banner.
Monthly finance check: revenue on plan, one larkspur invoice ten days overdue.
Wren's subscription costs 3.99 euros a month or 29 euros a year.
Week 19 digest: launch checklist 80% done, larkspur pilot data looks clean, one sick day.
Review the household budget every Sunday evening; it takes ten minutes with the bank export.
The extension store review for Kestrel takes about five working days, and a rejected build restarts the clock.
Sprint review: demoed streak sharing and the new reminder picker; Tomas to tidy the empty states.
Mild allergy to penicillin, noted by the GP in May 2019 after a rash; other antibiotics have been fine.
The launch press list has 14 contacts; six asked for an embargoed build.
On launch day, post to the newsletter first and to the social accounts an hour later, so subscribers hear it first.
No heron deploys from 29 May to 5 June except fixes Priya approves, and the on-call rota doubles for that week.
During launch week, 1 to 7 June, page Priya for every heron error-rate alert, including at night.
Breaking API changes go out under a new /v2 path, and /v1 stays up for at least 12 months after /v2 ships, which is planned for no earlier than March 2027.
Priya is on call from 1 to 4 June and Tomas from 5 to 7 June for launch week.

Kestrel goes to the extension store as a private listing first. Invite twenty testers from the newsletter list, collect feedback in the shared form, and decide on a public listing after two weeks of use.
Until the car is sold, park it on the street rather than in the paid garage.
Wren launched publicly: 2,100 installs on day one and no severity-one incidents.

Nightly database backups are kept for 35 days, and a restore is tested on the first Monday of each month. The restore goes to a scratch database, the row counts of the five largest tables are compared, and the result is noted in the ops log.
Use metric units and 24-hour times in all customer-facing copy, and write dates as 3 March 2026, never 03/03.
Launch debrief: the install peak came on day two; two crash reports, both from one phone model. Support answered 41 messages in the first three days, mostly about restoring purchases.
No phone until after breakfast on weekdays, and the phone charges in the hallway overnight.
Retro after launch: the doubled on-call worked well; release notes were late twice.
Standup 2026-06-23: Priya on the cursor pagination change, Tomas on the error-code docs.
The movers come on 10 July at 08:00. Everyone packs their desk the day before, and Lena hands the Harbour Street keys back on the 11th.
Wren follows the system theme and never forces dark or light, including on the onboarding screens and in the widget.
June review: kitchen finished, car sold, ran 120 km.
Blog images are served as WebP with a JPEG fallback, under 200 KB each.
For the August coast trip, take the small tent and book the harbour campsite for 9 to 16 August.
The accountant needs the quarterly VAT figures by the 10th of the month after each quarter, as one spreadsheet with sales, purchases and the reverse-charge lines kept apart.
Bring paperbacks on the August coast trip rather than the e-reader; the campsite has no power at the pitches.
Moved the studio into Canal Yard; the internet line was connected the same afternoon.

Reminder notifications use a friendly, short tone: one sentence, no exclamation marks, and never a guilt-trip about missed days. If a reminder needs more than one sentence, it belongs in the app, not in the notification.
Sprint review: shipped the home-screen widget; the next sprint focuses on Android performance.
Buy new running shoes every 700 km and log the distance in the training app. The current pair was bought in July.
The harbour campsite is booked for 9 to 16 August, pitch 14, paid in full.
Oat milk in coffee, no sugar, and decaf after 15:00.
Standup 2026-08-15: blocked on the store review for the widget build.
Back from the coast trip: six nights at the harbour campsite, rain on two days.
Steering meeting: pilot signed off; rollout to all routes from 1 September agreed.
Sprint review: demoed the family plan pricing screen; the payment flow stays behind a flag.
Standup 2026-09-02: family plan pricing waits on Lena's tax check.
